answer: Arrival-shape admission gate. Each new agent identity must generate traffic whose inter-arrival timing matches a wharf-like baseline distribution: bursts within a window are capped and smoothness is scored by the coefficient of variation of a ripple of requests. An identity opening too fast, or whose traffic lacks a natural jetty of pauses, is queued or rejected. Enforcement is per-identity, so an attacker spinning up N sybils must furnish each with plausible shaped traffic for a probation period, multiplying compute, IP rotation, and latency costs by N.
